note: Real CFP selection committee decisions, 12-team format. Ranks are the official final CFP rankings. Source links go to collegefootballplayoff.com.
rule: The five highest-ranked conference champions and the next seven highest-ranked teams make the field (CFP release, Dec. 7, 2025).

precedents.text: 2024: SMU (No. 10) lost the ACC title game and still made the field. Alabama (No. 11) was the first team out.
2024: Indiana (No. 8), with no title game, made the field as an at-large team. Miami (No. 13) did not.
2024: Texas (No. 3) and Penn State (No. 4) lost conference title games and stayed in the top four of the final rankings.
2024: ACC champion Clemson (No. 16) and Mountain West champion Boise State (No. 9) made the field as conference champions.
2024: Big 12 champion Arizona State (No. 12) made the field. BYU finished No. 17.
2025: Miami (No. 10) finished one spot ahead of Notre Dame (No. 11) and took the last at-large spot. Notre Dame was the first team out.
2025: BYU (No. 12) lost the Big 12 title game to Texas Tech (No. 4) and was left out. Utah finished No. 15.
2025: Tulane (No. 20) and James Madison (No. 24) made the field as the fourth and fifth highest-ranked conference champions. The ACC champion was not ranked.
2025: Alabama (No. 9) lost the SEC title game and stayed in the field.
2025: Seeds followed the final ranking. Ohio State (No. 2) lost the Big Ten title game and still got the No. 2 seed and a bye.

verified: All ranks checked against the official final CFP rankings pages on collegefootballplayoff.com, Oct. 23, 2026.
